text:
Samir K: on a support call now — Acme reported repeated mid-stream disconnects when generating long responses via SSE in our hosted API. iOS app: user switches from Wi-Fi to cellular mid-request and the client sees stream stop at ~60-70% of tokens. No 5xx from our side, but client logs show ECONNRESET and then no reconnect attempts. :confused:

Priya S: can you paste the request_id / any server logs? is it always iOS or mobile-only? any app version?

Samir K: request_id: r-0a1b2c3d4e5f (customer claim). iOS 16.4 / app 3.2.1. Happens on both wifi->cell and cell->wifi handovers. Customer sent snippet from device log: 
```
2024-10-12T14:02:13.425Z EVENTSTREAM connection established (req=r-0a1b2c3d4e5f)
2024-10-12T14:02:52.771Z NETWORK_CHANGE wifi -> cellular
2024-10-12T14:02:52.773Z TCP connection reset (errno=54)\n2024-10-12T14:02:52.775Z EVENTSTREAM client disconnected (code=ECONNRESET)
```

Nora M: interesting — iOS networking can drop sockets on interface switch. EventSource / SSE doesn't have built-in resume; browser JS reconnects but native clients often need logic. Does the server emit an "id:" field per event so clients can resume with Last-Event-ID?

Samir K: the generation stream currently writes non-deterministic chunked data, no id header for each token. We do emit final event id at end only. Customer's app code uses a plain TCP read and SSE parser, no resume implementation.

Liam R: From infra side, I checked ELB/ALB logs for r-0a1b2c3d4e5f — no 5xxs; the ALB shows a 200 then a client close. Idle timeout on ALB is 60s default; but this case is immediate on network flip so probably client-side close. Do we send keepalive comments? If not, a short keepalive every ~15s would help some mobile NATs and keep intermediate proxies happier.

Priya S: agree — quick mitigation: (1) push a small server-side change to emit comment keepalives (":\n") every 10s for streaming endpoints, (2) add an SSE-compatible "id:" event prefix every N tokens so clients can resume, and (3) document recommended client retry behavior (reopen and send Last-Event-ID).

Samir K: customer patch on their side is long lead; they asked if we can either (a) accept partial stream + new request to finish, or (b) support resume. Which is faster?

Nora M: resume requires deterministic event ids and idempotent continuation of model state — not trivial. For short term, sending keepalives is fastest. Also add logic to the client to retry on network change with a short backoff — they'll lose some tokens but at least get a second request to finish. We should provide a sample client snippet.

Samir K: sample curl to reproduce (attaching to thread):
```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=gpt-long&prompt=<<very long prompt>>"
```

Nora M: sample iOS EventSource-style reconnection pseudo-code to include in support guide:
```
// pseudo
let es = EventSource(url)
es.onmessage = { ev in processChunk(ev.data) }
es.onerror = { err in
  if networkChanged() {
    // reopen with Last-Event-ID if available
    reconnect(withLastEventId)
  }
}
```

Priya S: I'll also open an internal incident so Eng Infra can evaluate LB timeouts and connection drain behavior. @Liam can you check haproxy/nginx timeouts on edge nodes and whether we drop on interface-change vs keepalive? :eyes:

Liam R: on it. Quick findings: edge nginx has keepalive_timeout=75s and proxy_read_timeout=120s. proxy buffers are small; when client's TCP resets we see ECONNRESET on the upstream socket and the worker logs "upstream prematurely closed connection". That matches customer. I can test a keepalive comment patch in staging to see if proxies remain happy across an interface switch.

deploy-bot: canary release request created for commit 7f3a2b to deploy to staging and 1% traffic in prod.

Priya S: action list so far:
- Nora: add server-side SSE keepalive comments every 10s for streaming endpoints (staging PR).
- Nora + Runtime: add an optional per-event "id:" header design exploration (follow-up, needs model continuation design).
- Liam: test LB/edge behavior with keepalives and report results (1-2h).
- Samir: share client-side sample and customer logs, coordinate patch on customer side if they want retries.
- Priya: file an internal support KB with recommended client patterns + example code.

Samir K: pasted a short dump of the client's reconnection attempt (they tried to reopen immediately but the second response was empty):
```
client: reopen after ECONNRESET -> request sent
server: 200 OK, but stream immediately closed (0 bytes)
```

Nora M: that final empty response smells like an LB short-circuit when a stale connection attempt hits a closed socket. Keepalives should reduce prevalence. For the long-term resume story we need to ensure model output determinism or provide a server-side buffer+replay for a window (expensive).

Priya S: OK, please escalate severity to P2 for now (customer impact, reproducible). Samir — can you set expectations with Acme: we'll roll a keepalive change to staging within a few hours and request they try with their app (they're ok with testing).

Samir K: done — told them staging link + short repro steps. they're available for testing at 1700 PT.

Liam R: quick staging test results: with keepalive comments every 10s, the iOS app that previously dropped now stays connected through a wifi->cell switch in 3/3 tests. LB logs show continuous byte flow. Will prepare a one-off 1% prod canary.

Nora M: pushed PR to add keepalive comments (simple exporter wrapper):
```
// pseudocode inserted into stream loop
if timeSinceLastOutput > 10s {
  write(": keepalive\n\n")
  flush()
}
```
deploy-bot: canary started for 1% traffic (deploy 7f3a2b)

Samir K: customer confirmed 2 successful end-to-end tests with staging patch, improved UX. They're happy for canary to proceed. :thumbsup:

Priya S: closing notes: long-term: eval adding per-event ids and an optional resume API, and document recommended client behavior (reconnect/backoff/Last-Event-ID) in our streaming guide. For now keepalives + client retry guidance should mitigate most mobile handoffs. I'll convert this thread into a KB article and incident ticket.

inc-bot: incident INC-2024-847 created and linked to support ticket ST-9987.

Samir K: marking owners: Nora (server patch), Liam (infra test/canary), Priya (customer comms + KB), Samir (customer validation).

Priya S: thanks everyone. followup sync 1730 PT if issues show up. :heart:
